hed: Aspidiske: The Bright Beacon of Carina
dek: A detailed look at the luminous star situated in the constellation Carina, its significance, and observational highlights.
body:
Aspidiske, also known by its designation HIP 45556, is a prominent star located in the constellation Carina. Its celestial coordinates are approximately Right Ascension 9.28 hours and Declination -59.28 degrees, placing it in the southern sky. As a bright star with a notable presence, Aspidiske is often referenced in star charts and astronomical catalogues. It is considered a figure star or a candidate for physical object status within the stellar community, indicative of its significance in celestial mapping.

This star is part of a stellar grouping recognized in various star data collections, including the Hipparcos Catalogue, where it is listed with precise position data (RA: 9.2848412227 hours, Dec: -59.2752611500 degrees). Its brightness makes it accessible to amateur astronomers and serves as a useful reference point in the southerly skies. The luminosity of Aspidiske, although not specified here with an exact magnitude, is sufficient to distinguish it amidst the stellar backdrop. It is also associated with the cultural and navigational frameworks used historically in celestial navigation.

The star's significance extends beyond its brightness; it forms part of complex asterisms and is used as a reference in various star atlases and astronomical identifications. Its role in the constellation Carina contributes to understanding the structure of this part of the Milky Way's constellation pattern. Aspidiske's position and classification as a figure star highlight its utility in celestial navigation and positional astronomy.

Astronomers and star enthusiasts benefit from knowing the precise locations and identities of stars like Aspidiske, which aid in star-hopping, navigation, and understanding stellar evolution. While numerous details about its spectral type and physical properties await precision measurement, Aspidiske remains a key star in the southern celestial sphere—a luminous beacon for anyone exploring the rich tapestry of the night sky.
